title: EnsembleLink: Accurate Record Linkage Without Training Data
abstract: arXiv:2601.21138v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Record linkage, the process of matching records that refer to the same entity across datasets, is essential to empirical social science but remains methodologically underdeveloped. Researchers treat it as a preprocessing step, applying ad hoc rules without quantifying the uncertainty that linkage errors introduce into downstream analyses. Existing methods either achieve low accuracy or require substantial labeled training data. I present EnsembleLink, a method that achieves high accuracy without any training labels. EnsembleLink leverages pre-trained language models that have learned semantic relationships (e.g., that "South Ozone Park" is a neighborhood in "New York City" or that "Lutte ouvriere" refers to the Trotskyist "Workers' Struggle" party) from large text corpora. On benchmarks spanning city names, person names, organizations, multilingual political parties, and bibliographic records, EnsembleLink matches or exceeds methods

translated_title: EnsembleLink：无需训练数据的高精度记录链接
translated_abstract: 记录链接是指在数据集之间匹配指向同一实体的记录的过程，它对实证社会科学至关重要，但在方法论上仍发展不足。研究者通常将其视为预处理步骤，采用临时性的规则，却未量化链接错误给下游分析带来的不确定性。现有方法要么准确率较低，要么需要大量有标注的训练数据。本文提出EnsembleLink，一种无需任何训练标签即可实现高准确率的方法。EnsembleLink利用预训练语言模型，这些模型已从大规模文本语料中学习到语义关系（例如，"South Ozone Park"是"New York City"的一个社区，或"Lutte ouvriere"指托洛茨基主义的“工人斗争”党）。在涵盖城市名称、人名、组织机构、多语言政党及文献记录的基准测试中，EnsembleLink的表现与现有方法相当或更优。
tldr: 该论文提出EnsembleLink方法，利用预训练语言模型的语义理解能力，在完全不需要训练标签的情况下实现了高精度记录链接，其表现达到或超越现有方法。
